    File format

    Click the encoding, line ending or delimiter on the right of the status bar to open the CSV File Format dialog (TSV File Format for TSV files).

    Item Choices
    Encoding UTF-8, UTF-8 with BOM, UTF-16 LE/BE, Korean (CP949, EUC-KR), Japanese (Shift_JIS, EUC-JP), Chinese (GBK, GB18030, Big5), Windows 1252 and more
    Delimiter Comma, Tab, Semicolon, Colon, Pipe, Space, Other (type one character)
    Quote None, ", ', Other (type one character)
    Quote Mode Always, Minimal (only cells with the delimiter, a quote or a line break), Never
    Line Ending LF, CRLF
    Final Newline Whether the file ends with a line break

    Reopen and Apply

    • Reopen: reads the file from disk again in the chosen format. Unsaved edits are discarded. For example, a CP949 file that shows garbled text opens correctly after choosing Korean (CP949) and reopening.
    • Apply: keeps the cell values and changes only the format used when saving. It takes effect in the file when you save and can be undone.

    What is stored in .meta

    Anything that can't be detected from a BOM or the extension (a legacy encoding, or a non-default delimiter, quote or quote mode) is written to the file's .meta (userData). The file opens the same way next time and for teammates who get it through version control. When everything is default, the .meta is left unchanged.

    Note

    If another tool already uses the file's userData, Tabular Editor doesn't overwrite it and logs a warning in the Console.
